layers.name: Prompt
layers.what: A one-off structured instruction you paste into a conversation.

layers.name: Context file
layers.what: What the agent always knows about the initiative: how we work, the lifecycle, conventions, trace IDs, templates, ground rules and scale.
layers.tools: Many coding agents read AGENTS.md at the repository root. Tools with their own file (e.g. CLAUDE.md) can import or copy it. In chat assistants, paste it into the project's instructions.

layers.name: Skills
layers.what: Reusable how-to packages — one per technique or method — with steps, structure, output templates and checks. The agent loads one when the task needs it.
layers.tools: Agents that support skills load SKILL.md folders from their skills directory. Otherwise attach the SKILL.md as a file, or paste it before the prompt.

layers.name: Commands
layers.what: Saved prompts you run by name, with arguments — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act.
layers.tools: Agents with custom commands or saved prompts read Markdown files from their commands / prompts folder; $ARGUMENTS takes what you type after the name. Otherwise paste the file.

layers.name: Workflows
layers.what: A run specification: steps in order, inputs and outputs as files, who owns each step, human checkpoints, decision branches, recovery and the gate.
layers.tools: Point the agent at the workflow file ("run workflows/x.md, stop at every checkpoint"). Orchestration tools can execute the YAML block; people can read it as a checklist.

layers.name: Subagents
layers.what: Specialised helpers with one job — lens reviewers (privacy, security, finance…), a researcher, a synthesiser, a challenger, a decision-brief writer.
layers.tools: Agents that support subagents load them from their agents folder. Otherwise open a separate conversation and paste the file as its first message.

layers.name: Tools & connectors
layers.what: Which tools and data each step needs — web search, documents, spreadsheets, the backlog tool, the research repository, the code repository — and what each scale allows the agent to do with them.
layers.tools: Connect tools through your agent's connectors or MCP servers; grant the least access the step needs.

layers.name: Guardrails & hooks
layers.what: Rules the agent must follow and automatic checks at key moments — before saving an artifact, before a decision, before sending anything outside the team.
layers.tools: Agents with hooks can run these checks automatically; everywhere else they're a checklist the agent applies and you confirm.

layers.name: Rubrics
layers.what: A scored checklist for each artifact, from its template, quality criteria and the unit's criteria.

layers.name: Memory & handoff
layers.what: What carries across sessions and people: the project folder, a progress log, and a trace-ID register.
layers.tools: Keep them in the repository or shared drive the agent can read; start each session with "read PROGRESS.md".

scales.name: Solo / small
scales.who: One person or a small team of 2–5, each wearing several roles.

scales.name: Product team
scales.who: A cross-functional product team: product trio plus a delivery team of 5–10.

scales.name: Enterprise
scales.who: Many teams, formal governance, regulation, shared services and a portfolio board.

scales.name: Platform
scales.who: A team building shared capabilities — APIs, internal platforms, developer tools — for other teams.
